sources.title: Visit Visa / Entry Permit Requirements for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
sources.publisher: Immigration Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Immigration Department visitor-requirements chapter contains the current foreign-country/travel-document table, says it was updated in August 2026, and expressly gives its residual other-foreign-countries visitor cohort seven days. It also says a person who needs a visa or entry permit must obtain it before travelling.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nationals of other foreign countries do not require visas for a visit

sources.title: Entry Arrangements for Mainland, Macao, Taiwan & Overseas Chinese Residents
sources.publisher: Immigration Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Immigration Department page is revised 2 June 2026. It separately states Macao resident-card and Visit Permit concessions, Macao-SAR-passport transit, and Chinese-resident-of-Taiwan PAR and entry-permit arrangements; these rules do not use a generic foreign-passport schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Holders of Macao SAR passports and holders of Macao SAR Travel Permits may transit Hong Kong for a stay up to 7 days

sources.title: Immigration Facilitation Scheme for Invited Persons
sources.publisher: Immigration Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Immigration Department visitor-facilitation page expressly identifies Timor-Leste as an ASEAN member state from 26 October 2025. It independently confirms the Department's current country treatment for the positive other-foreign-countries residual; its invitation-only benefits are not used to determine the baseline.

policies.title: Timor-Leste ordinary passports: seven-day Hong Kong visitor waiver
policies.summary: Hong Kong Immigration's current visitor table expressly assigns nationals of other foreign countries to a visa-free visitor stay of up to seven days. Timor-Leste is classified only through that affirmative residual, not through absence from the named rows.
conditions: The express current residual is limited to a visit not exceeding seven days for the foreign-country passport cohort.
The current Immigration Department separately identifies Timor-Leste in a visitor-facilitation country table; that scheme's invitation-only benefits do not define this ordinary-passport baseline.

For work, study, establishing or joining a business, residence, or a visitor stay longer than the allowed visa-free period, the current Immigration Department guidance requires the appropriate visa or entry permit before travel.
Normal immigration requirements, funds, onward or return travel, passport validity, individual admission and security controls remain separate.

conflicts.explanation: The fallback's visa-free label cannot be supported for a Macao SAR ordinary passport alone. The current Immigration Department route splits Macao permanent-resident cards and Visit Permits from a passport-only seven-day transit concession; it does not establish a passport-only visitor waiver.

The fallback's advance-visa label cannot be made into one ordinary Taiwan-passport rule. The current Immigration Department route divides Taiwan cases by Chinese-resident status, residence, birth or prior-admission history, travel documents, conditional PAR and entry permits.

unresolved.reason: The current Immigration Department arrangements give entry-permit-free visits to specified Macao permanent-resident card or Visit Permit holders, and a separate 30-day Visit Permit route for certain non-permanent residents. A Macao SAR passport is expressly described only for qualifying seven-day transit with onward travel. Those resident, permit and transit rules do not establish a passport-only short-visitor baseline for the MO ordinary-passport code; the foreign-country residual is not used for Macao.

Current Immigration Department arrangements treat Chinese residents of Taiwan through purpose-specific entry permits, a conditional PAR route for people born in Taiwan or previously admitted as Taiwan residents, and a separate Mainland Travel Permit route. Those rules additionally depend on current residence, birth/admission history and other travel-document facts. They do not establish one ordinary Taiwan-passport visitor baseline, and the foreign-country residual is not used for Taiwan.

The current Immigration Department table has no direct Kosovo passport row. Its seven-day residual is expressly framed for nationals of other foreign countries, but the current Hong Kong materials reviewed provide no affirmative Kosovo-recognition or travel-document mapping to that cohort. Neither a waiver nor a pre-travel visa/entry-permit route is assigned from omission or an unproven residual scope.
